newsitem.title: USA: Poland needs work to qualify for EU - World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Poland needs work to qualify for EU - World Bank.

text.p: Poland needs tax and bank reforms, privatisation and a better investment climate to prepare the ground for membership in the European Union, the World Bank said in a report released on Wednesday.
The report, entitled "Poland: Reform and Growth on the Road to the EU", said sustained economic growth was essential for Poland to adopt the changes needed for European Union membership.
"Poland's ability to meet the accession criteria will largely depend on its economic performance," said World Bank country director Basil Kavalsky.

"Growth is a clear sign of a well-functioning market economy... Firm economic reforms which generate and sustain further growth will be the key for Poland to fulfil the requirements of EU membership."
The Polish economy grew some six percent last year and economists expect the expansion to continue in 1997 and 1998.
"Poland is a pace-setter in the transformation from socialism to a market economy," said the report.

But it added: "Poland still has a long way to go in structural reform... Speeding up the pace of reform is critical to increase domestic saving, reduce the vulnerability of public finances and maintain the dynamic supply response of the Polish economy."
The report said not all its Polish wish-list would be formal requirements of European Union membership, but said legal and institutional change would both be needed.
Competition laws should meet EU standards and judges needed to get to know EU rules and regulations.

Large-scale investment would be needed in infrastructure, especially to improve environmental standards, while privatisation should be accelerated to boost investment and growth and ease the burden on the budget.

"The bank's report aims to assist Poland to formulate an economic strategy, which will both sustain long-term economic growth and help the country fulfil the formal requirements of EU membership," regional World Bank chief economist Marcelo Selowsky said.

"The challenges of accession to the European Union offer unique incentives for Poland to further strengthen its economy and address the most urgent needs in the areas of social protection and environment."
